text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach detected in us-west-2 model-serving pool. Automated checks show tail stalls and increased stream reconnects. Paging @sara (oncall). Incident ID INC-2026-95321. Please triage and shout if customer-visible impact.

sara: on it. any quick impact numbers? which model(s) and which nodes are flaring?

ben: quick snapshot from metrics (1m ago): p95=320ms (ok), p99=2.9s (SLO 1s), streaming reconnects +120% last 5m, inflight queue depth increased ~3x. Top host by error rate: gpu-node-47.us-west-2 (pool=model-serving-1).

ben: logs show repeated 'stream stalled, retrying' entries and some hardware correctable error counts rising. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T18:54:33Z] stream: stall detected id=abc123 duration=1800ms host=gpu-node-47
[2026-03-15T18:54:34Z] hwmon: ecc_correctable_inc host=gpu-node-47 counter=42
[2026-03-15T18:54:35Z] gpu: thermal_throttle_count=3 power=320W fan=85% host=gpu-node-47
```

nirav: running quick `kubectl` checks now.

k8s-bot: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47` -> 24 pods, 8 streaming workers (model=chat-stream-v2). Node CPU 35%, GPU util 62%, but NVML reports intermittent resets.

nirav: agreed with ben, looks like hardware-level instability on gpu-node-47 (correctable ECC spikes + thermal events). Suggest cordon+drain that node and failover streaming workers to warm spare pool. If drain looks long, scale up additional replicas of the streaming deployment to absorb tail.

sara: ok please do cordon+drain. prioritize streaming workers first and leave infra-critical pods alone. include `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` flags.

nirav: running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

ben: started evicting pods, streaming workers show graceful reconnects to other nodes. traffic to model-serving-1 dropped ~25% on gpu-node-47 as pods terminated.

ben: also triggered autoscaler to add 2 nodes in us-west-2 warm pool (policy=fast-failover).

joe: taking handoff from sara for oncall shift change — will own follow-ups and comms. @sara can you paste any customer-facing notes? I'll coordinate hardware ops.

sara: customer impact so far: a small subset (~2.4% of traffic routed to gpu-node-47) experienced increased p99 and occasional truncated streams for 3-6s before reconnect. No widespread errors in non-streaming endpoints. I drafted a short status for support: "Short live-stream interruptions for a subset of requests in US-West; mitigation in progress, we're draining a degraded GPU node and routing traffic to healthy capacity."

joe: got it. I'll notify hardware runbook and request a physical node check for ECC logs and thermal sensors. I'll also keep model fallback enabled to quantized variant if reconnections persist.

ben: a quick NVML snapshot while drain progressed:
```
GPU 0: ecc_correctable = 0 -> 49 over 6m
GPU 0: thermal_slowdowns = 2
Driver: nvidia-525.89.02
node_pci_errors: some correctable parity events
```

nirav: this looks like a flakey DIMM or thermal boundary causing repeated correctable errors, which triggers micro-pauses in SM scheduling -> streaming stalls. Node-level mitigation: isolate, replace, or run memtest. Short-term: keep node cordoned and out of rotation.

sara: marking incident severity as Sev2 (customer impact limited but SLO breached for p99 streaming). Starting an incidents slack thread doc: assign postmortem after stabilization.

incident-bot: Update: incident INC-2026-95321 status=mitigating, impacted_customers=~2.4%, mitigation=drained node & scaled warm pool, next_update=+15m.

joe: I already opened HW ticket HT-7602 and asked datacenter ops to snapshot BIOS and sensor logs. I'll follow up on trace correlation to confirm if any specific model shard had higher error rates.

ben: cluster-level alerting rule tuned: add short cooldown to correctable-ecc anomaly detectors so we don't flip on transient single-gpu blips, but keep alerting for repeated >10/min. Will propose thresholds in postmortem.

nirav: follow-up actions I recommend:
- keep gpu-node-47 cordoned and off autoscaling pools
- run memtest overnight after node cold-boot
- replace DIMM if memtest fails or if ECC counters don't drop after cold start
- validate streaming worker reconnect logic for edge-case stalls (add jitter/backoff)

sara: all captured. joe, you're primary for customer comms, ben + nirav for infra/running tests. i'll update support with the draft note and tag affected customers.

joe: taking ownership. thanks all. please react with :thumbsup: when done with assigned tasks in the next 20m so I can close mitigation phase in the incident tracker.

incident-bot: Automated reminder: create postmortem ticket with tag #gpu-hardware and include metrics: p95/p99 timeline, affected hosts, drain time, ECC counters.

sara: :thumbsup: closing my immediate oncall loop, leaving handoff to joe.

ben: :thumbsup: pods evicted, node drained, warm pool up +2. I'll watch for regression in the next 30m.

joe: logging the incident now and will post an ops summary in 1h. if anything flares, re-ping me directly.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-95321 closed->mitigating->postmortem_planned.
